To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

colleges that have a student-centered mission, a culture that supports that mission, a curriculum that challenges students, and a cocurriculum that supports students in their learning and development, have students who are satisfied with their educational experience and are developing holistically.

colleges and universities can become and remain more student centered by developing and implementing a holistic student development approach that includes a culture that is consistent with the institution's mission; a curriculum that is intellectually challenging and that provides students with opportunities to explore the nature of knowledge, life, and self; a cocurriculum that provides opportunities to explore and develop the whole person, including the mind, the spirit, and the body; and a campus community that is supportive of students' efforts to develop as whole persons.

institutions can become and remain student-centered by developing an institutional culture that is holistic and by using the curriculum, cocurricula, and community to foster and support holistic student development.

how institutions can help students learn more effectively about who they are and how they want to be in the world (p. 59).
